Subject: Model fit & safety evals — follow-up and next steps

Hi Emily —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking through HealthScope's primary use cases and the sample transcripts. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- Goal: generate clinical-summarization and triage suggestions from intake transcripts while ensuring PHI-safe handling and conservative refusal behaviors for diagnosis/off-label advice.
- Priority constraints: HIPAA-safe deployment (audit logs + KMS), deterministic refusal for sensitive prompts, and stable quality vs. current in-house model.

Preliminary model recommendations
- Redwood-13B-quant (fast, low-cost) — good for triage-level summaries and high throughput.
- Falcon-40B or Llama2-70B (quantized) — better for nuanced clinical language and safety-sensitive refusal accuracy.
- We recommend testing 13B for latency/cost and 40B/70B for quality/safety tradeoffs.

Evals & artifacts I'm sharing
- Link to benchmark suite: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/healthcare-evals-2026 (also attached as model_benchmarks_link.txt)
- Prompt set + seed cases: Drive folder (attached link) and sample prompts file (healthscope_sample_prompts.json).
- Our quick safety summary PDF: redwood_safety_eval_summary.pdf (attached) — contains example refusal prompts and measured failure modes.

Immediate next steps
1) We’ll run an initial model-fit eval on the 200 sample transcripts you shared under the NDA scope — can you confirm we have permission to ingest those?
2) Redwood security will run a targeted safety/refusal evaluation focusing on diagnosis, medication advice, and PHI leakage. We recommend a 2-week internal eval cadence for the first pass.
3) Technical sync (30 min) with your SRE/procurement to discuss deployment options (Hosted vs. Private/HIPAA) — propose Wed 6/17 or Thu 6/18.

Can you confirm permission to ingest the sample transcripts and which date/time works for the technical sync?

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your priorities.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Emily —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers up front, then proposed plan: 

1) Concrete failure cases (examples)
- Case A: model produced a confident medication dosage recommendation when prompt included partial medication history — occurred on a 13B baseline in our internal benchmark. The failure was tied to prompt engineering and lack of a policy filter; after adding a hard refusal trigger for dosage requests and improving system instruction, the failure rate dropped ~85%.
- Case B: model hallucinated a specific drug contraindication for a hypothetical comorbidity — observed in a single-shot eval on a 40B finetune. Mitigation: additional targeted few-shot examples and model variant selection (prefer L2-70B quant for conservative factuality).

2) Data retention
- By default, hosted eval ingestion is transient: raw inputs + logs retained for 30 days, eval artifacts retained 90 days. For HealthScope pilot we can set a 30-day max for raw inputs and agreed deletion of intermediate artifacts on completion. For longer-term, we recommend Redwood Private deployment (customer-controlled storage + KMS) to meet HIPAA requirements.

3) Pricing ballpark for pilot
- Pilot (250k tokens/month + safety eval services): approx $6k/month for hosted infra + one-time $12k for the safety/red-team eval and report. We’ll send a formal SOW/quote ahead of your 6/22 SOW review.

Proposed plan
- Task A (this week): confirm ingestion permission and sign minimal data use addendum (I’ll attach a short DUO after this thread).
- Task B (next 10 business days): Redwood runs model-fit and safety/refusal eval across 13B and 40B candidates and returns a scored report (we’ll include per-prompt failure types).
- Task C (after pilot): recommend model variant for production and deployment mode (hosted vs private) based on cost/quality/safety tradeoffs.

For the tech sync Wed 6/17 11:00am PT — I’ll invite our infra lead (Dylan) and Marissa (model eval lead) to join.

Action items for HealthScope: confirm permission to ingest the 200 transcripts and sign the data use addendum (I’ll send DUO by EOD).

Best,
Rafael

Attachments: proposed DUO (to follow)

2) Model-fit eval (Marissa) — run 13B + 40B candidates on the provided 200 transcripts, measure ROUGE/ROUGE-L, hallucination rate, and a safety-failure taxonomy per prompt.
3) Safety/refusal testing (Neha) — targeted probe suite for diagnosis/medication/PHI leakage; produce refusal precision/recall and example failure cases (for Emily).
4) Delivery & SOW (Rafael) — formal quote and DUO to HealthScope; align pricing with sales.
